easy.def: Very cold, or very slow.
examples: The glacial water.
A glacial pace.
Glacial winds.

more.def: Extremely cold, or moving very slowly like a glacier.
examples: We swam in the glacial water.
The traffic moved at a glacial pace.
Glacial winds blew across the ice.

easy.def: A huge, slow river of ice.
examples: The glacier is made of ice.
We saw a glacier.
The glacier moves slowly.

more.def: A very large mass of ice that moves slowly over land.
examples: The glacier slowly slid down the mountain.
A glacier carved the valley long ago.
Tourists took a boat to see the glacier.

easy.def: Happy about something.
examples: I am glad you came.
She was glad it stopped raining.
We are glad to see you.

more.def: Happy and pleased about something.
examples: I'm glad that we finished before the storm started.
She was glad to find her lost mitten.
The family was glad to be home after the long trip.

easy.def: To make someone happy.
examples: The news gladdened her.
A song gladdened us.
It gladdens my heart.

more.def: To make someone feel glad or happy.
examples: The good news gladdened her.
A cheerful song gladdened the sad child.
It gladdens my heart to see you.

easy.def: An open place in a forest.
examples: We had a picnic in the glade.
A deer stood in the glade.
The glade was sunny.

more.def: A small open space with grass in a forest.
examples: A deer stepped into the sunny glade.
We found a quiet glade where we ate lunch.
Flowers grew in the glade among the tall trees.

easy.def: In a happy and willing way.
examples: I will gladly help.
She gladly shared.
He gladly came.

more.def: With happiness or a willingness.
examples: I will gladly help you carry the boxes.
She gladly shared her snack.
He gladly came to our party.

easy.def: Fancy and exciting.
examples: She wore a glamorous dress.
It was a glamorous party.
The glamorous movie star waved.

more.def: Exciting and fancy, in a way that makes people admire it.
examples: She wore a glamorous gown covered in sparkling beads to the school play.
The glamorous party had colorful lights and music.
Being a movie star sounds glamorous, but it also takes a lot of hard work.

easy.def: A fancy, exciting look that is very pretty.
examples: She loves the glamour of the stage.
The party had lots of glamour.
The movie star had glamour.

more.def: A special, exciting beauty that makes a person or place seem fancy and wonderful.
examples: The theater lit up with the glamour of an opening night.
She dreamed of the glamour of being a movie star.
The princess's gown had a glamour that made everyone stare.

easy.def: To take a quick look.
examples: I glance at the clock.
She glanced at me and smiled.
I glance out the window.

more.def: To look at something quickly and then look away.
examples: She glanced at her watch to check the time.
The driver glanced in the mirror before changing lanes.
He glanced over the menu and ordered quickly.

easy.def: A part of the body that makes something the body needs.
examples: A gland makes spit in your mouth.
Glands help the body work.
The gland makes tears.

more.def: A part of the body that makes a substance the body needs, such as sweat, saliva, tears or hormones.
examples: The glands in your mouth make saliva to help you chew and swallow.
A gland near your eye makes tears that keep your eyes wet.
The doctor felt the glands in his neck to see if he was getting a cold.

easy.def: A very bright light that hurts your eyes.
examples: The glare of the sun.
I squinted at the glare.
The glare was bright.

more.def: A strong, bright light that hurts your eyes, or an angry, hard look.
examples: I squinted against the glare of the sun on the snow.
The teacher gave a glare when we talked too loudly.
Sunglasses cut down the glare on the lake.

easy.def: To look at someone in an angry way.
examples: She glared at him.
He glared at the dog.
Don't glare.

more.def: To stare at someone in an angry way.
examples: She glared at her brother when he broke her toy.
The cat glared at the dog from the fence.
He glared at the clock, wishing school would end.

easy.def: A hard material you can see through.
examples: The window is glass.
The jar is glass.
Glass can break.

more.def: A hard, clear material that breaks easily, used for windows and cups.
examples: The windows are made of glass.
Be careful of broken glass.
A glass bottle sat on the shelf.

easy.def: A cup for drinking that you can see through.
examples: A glass of milk.
Fill the glass.
I broke a glass.

more.def: A clear cup for drinking, often without a handle.
examples: She poured a glass of juice.
He drank a tall glass of water.
A glass sat on the table.

easy.def: Things you wear on your face to see better.
examples: Dad wears glasses.
I lost my glasses.
Her glasses are blue.

more.def: Two clear lenses in a frame that people wear to see better.
examples: She put on her glasses to read the menu.
He wears glasses when he reads.
The teacher cleaned her glasses.

related.def: As much as a glass can hold.

easy.def: A building made of glass for growing plants.
examples: We grow tomatoes in the glasshouse.
The glasshouse is warm.
Plants grow in the glasshouse.

more.def: A building with glass walls and roof, used for growing plants.
examples: Tomatoes grew in the warm glasshouse.
The glasshouse trapped the sun's heat.
She watered the plants in the glasshouse.

easy.def: Things made of glass.
examples: She washed the glassware.
The glassware is clear.
Glassware breaks.

more.def: Cups and bowls of glass.
examples: She washed the glassware by hand.
The glassware sparkled on the shelf.
Be careful with the glassware.

easy.def: A shiny coating on food or pottery.
examples: The cake has a sweet glaze.
A glaze on the pot is shiny.
The doughnut had a glaze.

more.def: A thin, shiny coating put on food or pottery.
examples: The doughnut had a sweet sugar glaze.
The potter put a blue glaze on the bowl.
A honey glaze covered the ham.

easy.def: To cover something with a shiny coating.
examples: She will glaze the cake.
He glazed the pot.
Mom glazed the ham.

more.def: To cover food or pottery with a shiny coating.
examples: Mom glazed the ham with honey.
The potter glazed each bowl before baking it.
She glazed the cookies with sugar.

easy.def: Shiny with a coating.
examples: The doughnut is glazed.
I saw a glazed pot.
I like a glazed ham.

more.def: Covered with a shiny coating.
examples: The glazed doughnut was sticky and sweet.
The glazed pot shone in the light.
We ate a glazed carrot with dinner.

easy.def: To shine brightly.
examples: The stars gleam.
Her eyes gleamed.
The floor gleamed.

more.def: To shine brightly, often after being polished.
examples: The new coins gleamed in the sun.
The floor gleamed after it was cleaned.
The stars gleamed in the dark sky.

easy.def: A soft shine of light.
examples: A gleam of light shone.
I saw a gleam in the dark.
There was a gleam in her eye.

more.def: A bright flash or soft shine of light.
examples: A gleam of light came from under the door.
There was a happy gleam in her eye.
The gleam of the silver spoon caught my eye.

easy.def: Shining brightly.
examples: The car is gleaming.
A gleaming floor.
The gleaming coin.

more.def: Shining brightly and smoothly.
examples: The car was gleaming after the wash.
The gleaming floor reflected the light.
A gleaming coin sat on the table.

easy.def: To pick up bit by bit.
examples: She gleaned the facts.
He gleaned the grain.
They glean information.

more.def: To gather information or facts bit by bit; or to pick up grain left after the harvest.
examples: She gleaned a few facts from the old letter.
Farmers gleaned the leftover wheat.
He gleaned the answer from the clues.

easy.def: Great joy.
examples: The children shouted with glee.
She clapped with glee.
He laughed with glee.

more.def: A feeling of great joy and delight.
examples: The children shouted with glee in the snow.
She clapped her hands in glee at the surprise.
He laughed with glee when he saw the puppy.

easy.def: In a very happy way.
examples: The kids ran gleefully.
She gleefully clapped.
He gleefully jumped.

more.def: In a joyful way, often because something fun is happening.
examples: The children gleefully splashed in the puddles.
She gleefully tore open the present.
The puppy gleefully chased the ball.

easy.def: A small valley between hills.
examples: We walked through the glen.
The glen is green.
A stream ran in the glen.

more.def: A narrow valley, especially in Scotland or Ireland.
examples: A stream ran through the quiet glen.
We hiked through a misty glen.
Deer grazed in the glen.

easy.def: To move smoothly and easily.
examples: The swan glided on the lake.
I glided on the ice.
The bird glides in the air.

more.def: To move along smoothly and quietly, without effort or jerks.
examples: The swan glided across the still lake without a sound.
An eagle glided high above the valley on the warm air.
She glided across the ice in her skates.

easy.def: A plane with no engine that floats on the wind.
examples: The glider flew.
A glider has no motor.
We saw a glider.

more.def: A light aircraft without an engine that floats and soars on the wind.
examples: A glider floated silently over the hills.
The glider rode the wind high into the sky.
She dreams of flying a glider someday.

easy.def: A small, faint light.
examples: A glimmer of light shone.
I saw a glimmer.
There was a glimmer in the dark.

more.def: A faint, flickering light, or a small sign of hope.
examples: A glimmer of light came from the cabin.
There was a glimmer of hope as the sky cleared.
The glimmer of the stars lit the path.

easy.def: To shine with a faint, flickering light.
examples: The stars glimmer.
The lake glimmered.
The candle glimmered.

more.def: To shine with a faint, soft, flickering light.
examples: The stars glimmered in the sky.
The lake glimmered in the moonlight.
A candle glimmered in the window.

easy.def: A very quick look.
examples: I caught a glimpse of a deer.
He got a glimpse of the cake.
We had a glimpse of the stage.

more.def: A very quick look at something.
examples: I caught a glimpse of a deer in the woods.
He got a glimpse of the surprise before it was hidden.
We had a glimpse of the sea through the trees.

easy.def: To see something for just a moment.
examples: I glimpsed a fox.
She glimpsed the star.
We glimpsed the bird.

more.def: To see something for a very short time.
examples: I glimpsed a fox at the edge of the woods.
She glimpsed a shooting star across the sky.
We glimpsed a bird before it flew away.

easy.def: A quick flash of light.
examples: I saw a glint.
A glint of gold.
There was a glint in her eye.

more.def: A small, quick flash of light.
examples: I saw a glint of gold in the sand.
A glint of sun shone off the knife.
There was a happy glint in her eye.

easy.def: To shine like something wet.
examples: The dew will glisten.
The snow glistened.
The lake glistens.

more.def: To shine with a wet or sparkling light.
examples: The dew glistened on the grass.
The snow glistened in the sun.
The lake glistens in the morning.

easy.def: A small problem that stops something working.
examples: There was a glitch in the game.
The glitch fixed itself.
A glitch stopped the clock.

more.def: A small problem or fault that stops something from working right.
examples: A glitch in the game made the screen freeze.
A computer glitch made the lights flicker.
The glitch was easy to fix.

easy.def: Tiny, shiny bits that sparkle.
examples: I put glitter on my card.
The glitter is gold.
Glitter got on my hands.

more.def: Tiny, shiny pieces of paper or plastic that sparkle in the light, used for crafts and decorations.
examples: We sprinkled glitter on the glue to make our cards sparkle.
The costume was covered in silver glitter.
Glitter got all over the floor after the art class.

easy.def: To shine with little flashes of light.
examples: The stars glitter.
The snow glittered.
Her ring glitters.

more.def: To shine with many small, bright flashes of light.
examples: The frozen lake glittered in the morning sun.
The stars glittered in the dark sky.
Jewels glittered in the king's crown.

easy.def: To show off in a mean way about winning.
examples: Do not gloat when you win.
He gloated about his win.
She gloated over her score.

more.def: To show too much pleasure about your own success or about someone else's bad luck.
examples: Do not gloat when you win a game; it is kinder to say "good game."
He gloated about his high score until his friend felt sad.
The fox gloated over the stolen grapes.

easy.def: A small blob of wet or sticky stuff.
examples: A glob of paint fell.
He dropped a glob of jam.
A glob of mud.

more.def: A small, thick, soft lump of something wet or sticky.
examples: A glob of paint dripped from the brush.
He plopped a glob of jam on his toast.
A glob of mud splashed on my boot.

easy.def: All over the world.
examples: It is a global problem.
The global trip.
A global company.

more.def: Having to do with the whole world.
examples: Pollution is a global problem.
The company has global offices.
They took part in a global event.

easy.def: A ball with a map of the earth.
examples: I spin the globe.
The globe shows the world.
The globe is round.

more.def: A round model of the earth with the countries drawn on it.
examples: I spun the globe and pointed to Brazil.
The globe sat on the teacher's desk.
We found Africa on the globe.

easy.def: Shaped like a globe or ball.
examples: The lamp was globular.
A globular lamp.
The globular fruit.

more.def: Round like a ball.
examples: The lamp had a globular shade.
The globular fruit hung from the branch.
The jar was globular.

easy.def: A tiny round drop.
examples: A globule of oil.
The globule rolled.
A globule of water.

more.def: A tiny round drop or ball of a liquid.
examples: A globule of oil floated on the soup.
A globule of water shone on the leaf.
The mercury formed a silver globule.

easy.def: Darkness, or a sad feeling.
examples: We sat in the gloom.
A gloom filled the room.
The gloom lifted.

more.def: Darkness or dimness, or a feeling of sadness.
examples: We sat in the gloom of the cave.
A sense of gloom settled over the rainy day.
The gloom lifted when the sun came out.

easy.def: In a sad and unhappy way.
examples: He gloomily looked at the rain.
She gloomily sat down.
The boy gloomily left.

more.def: In a sad, dark or hopeless way.
examples: He gloomily stared out at the rain.
She gloomily dragged her feet on the way to school.
The team gloomily left the field after losing.

easy.def: Dark and sad.
examples: It is a gloomy, rainy day.
The cave was gloomy.
He felt gloomy when his friend left.

more.def: Dark and dull, or feeling sad and without hope.
examples: The gloomy old house had not seen sunlight in years.
Everyone felt gloomy after the team lost the final game.
The sky was gloomy all week, with no sign of the sun.

easy.def: Wonderful and bright.
examples: It was a glorious day.
The sunset was glorious.
We had a glorious time.

more.def: Very beautiful, bright or splendid.
examples: It was a glorious sunny day for the picnic.
The sunset was a glorious red.
The team celebrated a glorious win.

easy.def: Great honor for doing something amazing.
examples: The winner was covered in glory.
He won glory in the race.
The team enjoyed its glory.

more.def: Great honor and praise that comes from doing something amazing.
examples: The explorers returned home with glory.
The team won glory by winning the cup.
Soldiers in the old story fought for glory.

easy.def: A smooth, shiny look.
examples: The paint has a gloss.
The gloss is bright.
Lip gloss is shiny.

more.def: A smooth, shiny surface or look, or a shiny product put on lips or nails.
examples: The floor had a smooth gloss after it was polished.
She put clear gloss on her lips.
The car's gloss shone in the sunlight.

easy.def: A list of words and their meanings.
examples: Look in the glossary.
The glossary has words.
The glossary is at the back.

more.def: A list of difficult words and what they mean, usually at the back of a book.
examples: I looked up the word in the glossary.
The book has a glossary at the back.
The glossary explains hard words.

easy.def: Smooth and shiny.
examples: The paper is glossy.
A glossy coat.
The glossy apple shone.

more.def: Smooth and shiny on the surface.
examples: The photo was printed on glossy paper.
The dog had a glossy coat.
The glossy apple shone in the sun.

easy.def: A cover for your hand with a place for each finger.
examples: I wear gloves in the snow.
One glove is lost.
Put on your glove.

more.def: A covering for the hand with a separate place for each finger.
examples: She wore warm gloves to build the snowman.
The catcher put on a leather glove.
Dad wears gloves when he works in the garden.

easy.def: To give off a soft light.
examples: My night-light glows in the dark.
The stars glow at night.
The fire glows red.

more.def: To shine with a soft, steady light.
examples: The campfire glowed long after the flames died down.
Fireflies glowed in the dark field.
Her face glowed with happiness.

easy.def: A small bug that shines in the dark.
examples: A glowworm glows.
The glowworm shines at night.
I saw a glowworm.

more.def: A small insect or larva that gives off a greenish light in the dark.
examples: A glowworm glowed on the cave wall.
Glowworms give off a soft green light.
We saw glowworms in the cave.

easy.def: A sugar that gives your body energy.
examples: Glucose is sugar.
The body uses glucose.
Fruit has glucose.

more.def: A simple sugar that is the main source of energy for living things.
examples: Your body turns food into glucose.
Plants make glucose from sunlight.
Glucose gives your muscles energy.

easy.def: A sticky stuff that holds things together.
examples: I use glue on my paper.
The glue is sticky.
I need glue.

more.def: A sticky substance used to stick things together.
examples: I used glue to stick the paper onto the card.
The glue dried quickly.
He repaired the cup with glue.

easy.def: To stick things together.
examples: I glue the pieces.
She glued the cup.
He glued the paper.

more.def: To fasten things together using something sticky.
examples: I glued the pieces of the puzzle together.
She glued the handle back on the cup.
He glued pictures onto the board.

easy.def: Sticky like glue.
examples: The paste was gluey.
My fingers are gluey.
A gluey mess.

more.def: Sticky and thick.
examples: The paste was gluey and hard to wash off.
My fingers were gluey after the craft.
The rice turned gluey.

easy.def: Sad and quiet.
examples: The boy looked glum.
She was glum.
He was glum about the rain.

more.def: Sad, quiet and in a low mood.
examples: The glum boy sat alone at the table.
She felt glum when the picnic was canceled.
He was glum after losing the game.

easy.def: In a sad and quiet way.
examples: He sat glumly.
She glumly watched the rain.
The boy glumly packed up.

more.def: In a gloomy, sad way, without talking much.
examples: He sat glumly on the bench after losing.
She glumly watched the rain through the window.
The boy glumly packed up his toys.

easy.def: A protein found in wheat.
examples: Bread has gluten.
Gluten is in wheat.
She avoids gluten.

more.def: A sticky protein found in wheat and some other grains.
examples: Bread has gluten in it.
Some people cannot eat gluten.
The label said gluten-free.

easy.def: A carved picture symbol.
examples: A glyph is a symbol.
The wall had a glyph.
I drew a glyph.

more.def: A symbol or picture that stands for a sound or word, often carved in stone.
examples: Ancient people carved a glyph into the stone.
The Maya wrote with glyphs.
